blinding_guess.why: Both scripts use the five rospy symbols in the conventional ROS 1 way: init_node with anonymous=True, Subscriber(topic, type, callback), Publisher(topic, type, queue_size=10), spin(), and catching ROSInterruptException; queue_size is already passed to every Publisher, and rospy is listed as build and run dependency. Nothing in the snapshot suggests a mismatch with the indigo rospy API.

notes: ROS 1 (indigo), so all QoS fields are null. The five packet elements are rospy API symbols that kobuki_node consumes only in its two Python helper scripts, scripts/getOdom2D.py and scripts/getYaw.py (installed via CMakeLists.txt:33-36); the C++ nodelet (src/library, src/nodelet) uses roscpp, not rospy. rospy is declared at package.xml:45 (build_depend) and package.xml:78 (run_depend) under a 'For Tests' comment, and in CMakeLists.txt:3 and :11. Because the elements are API symbols rather than data ports, msg_type, frame, units, rate and definition_id are null (no .msg/.srv definition applies). The rospy API signatures themselves could not be checked against the indigo rospy source, which is outside the allowed sources. declares and not_declared are empty because every packet element is consumed, not provided. Non-packet interface items seen in the same scripts and deliberately not listed in references: getOdom2D.py subscribes to relative topic 'odom' (nav_msgs/Odometry) and publishes 'pose2d' (geometry_msgs/Pose2D); getYaw.py subscribes to 'imu' (sensor_msgs/Imu) and publishes 'angle' and 'angle_rate' (std_msgs/Float64); launch/test_get_odom.launch and launch/test_get_yaw.launch remap these names. Both scripts also call roslib.load_manifest('kobuki_node') and use Python 2 print statements. exclusive is left empty: param/base.yaml:5 sets device_port: /dev/kobuki, which kobuki_ros.cpp:145 reads and hands to kobuki_driver (not in the snapshot); the snapshot code does not itself claim that device exclusively, so no exclusivity is recorded. Recovery: param/base.yaml:20-21 documents a cmd_vel_timeout after which the base is stopped, and kobuki_ros.cpp says a missing data stream can be 'resurrected' by turning kobuki on while spinning; neither is a declared recovery policy, so recovery is recorded as absent.
